default.notes: Vatican City issues no visas of its own — entry is through Italy, so a Schengen short-stay visa issued for Italy is required.

groups.notes: Entry is via Italy: EU citizens reach Vatican City freely under Schengen rules, and there are no checks at the Vatican boundary.
EFTA citizens enter via Italy under free-movement rules; there are no Vatican border checks.
90 days in any 180-day period under Schengen rules, entered through Italy — the Vatican itself has no border controls. ETIAS will apply once mandatory.
Visa-free with a biometric passport under Schengen rules (90 days in any 180), entered through Italy; the Vatican itself has no border controls.
Visa-free with a biometric passport under Schengen rules (90 days in any 180), entered through Italy; the Vatican itself has no border controls.

VA.notes: Home state — Vatican citizens and Holy See passport holders enter freely.

IT.notes: Vatican City is an enclave within Rome — Italian citizens cross freely with no checks of any kind.

UA.notes: Visa-free with a biometric passport under Schengen rules (90 days in any 180), entered through Italy.

RU.notes: A Schengen short-stay visa issued for Italy is required. The EU suspended its visa facilitation agreement with Russia; fees are higher and processing slower.

VU.notes: The EU suspended Vanuatu's visa waiver over its citizenship-by-investment scheme; a Schengen visa issued for Italy is required.
